title: An Efficient Machine Learning-based Framework for Detection and Prevention of Frauds in Telecom Networks
summary: Telecom fraud causes large financial losses and needs scalable, accurate detection; the paper evaluates machine-learning classifiers on a Call Detail Record (CDR) dataset with 101,174 customer records, 17 attributes and 8,830 fraud cases. The pipeline removes records with missing values, applies Min-Max scaling (Eq. 1), balances classes with SMOTE, splits 80/20 into train/test, and fits Random Forest and XGBoost models, which are also compared against reported DBSCAN, RoBERTa and K-means baselines using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and ROC AUC. Random Forest is reported as the best model with 99.9% accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score (XGBoost 99.7% accuracy and 99.8% on the other metrics), and the RF confusion matrix shows 26,127 TP, 273,871 TN, 0 FP and 2 FN.

match_target.why: Random Forest accuracy of 99.9% is the paper's headline result and the user's stated target; it needs only one scikit-learn RandomForest fit on a small tabular dataset after missing-value removal, Min-Max scaling and SMOTE (no GPU, no deep model, no baselines), so it is by far the cheapest claim that still demonstrates the central finding.

tolerance.why: Rule 2: the target is an accuracy-like percentage with no reported std or CI, and the evaluated test set is far larger than 2,000 examples (the paper's confusion matrix sums to 300,000 predictions), so the band is 1.0 absolute point (98.9-100)%.
